title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed, mimeographed Bourbaki draft: the header reads '4 - 37 -' and 'n° 392', the typescript is in blue duplicator ink, and only the archive foliation '53' is handwritten. Grothendieck evidently used the back of Bourbaki drafts as scratch paper for his notes on the functional equation of L-functions; the neighbouring pages are his handwritten notes. The text belongs to the draft of Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, Chap. VII (Diviseurs), §4 on finitely generated modules over Krull domains, at the point where the behaviour of the 'content' χ under integral extensions is treated (n° 8 in the published version, 1965).

Setting. A is a Krull domain with fraction field K; L is a finite extension of K; B is the integral closure of A in L. B is again a Krull domain.
- D(A) is the divisor group, the free group on P(A), the height-one primes of A.
- For a finitely generated torsion module M, χ_A(M) = Σ_p length_{A_p}(M_p)·p.
- i: D(A) → D(B) is the extension of divisors, i(p) = Σ_{P|p} e(P/p)·P.
- A module is pseudo-null if its localizations at all height-one primes vanish.

The page finishes three arguments.

(1) End of Lemma 4: if f: M → N is an injective map of A-modules, then I = Ker(f⊗1_B) is pseudo-null.
- Kernels commute with localization, so I_p = Ker((f⊗1)_p).
- For p of height one, A_p is a DVR and B_p is finite and torsion-free over it, hence free, hence flat. So (f⊗1)_p is injective and I_p = 0.
- Hence I_P = (I_p)_P = 0 for every height-one P of B lying over p.

(2) Proof of (ii): χ_B(M⊗_A B) = i(χ_A(M)) for finitely generated torsion M.
- Set φ(M) = χ_B(M⊗_A B). By (i), φ vanishes on pseudo-null modules.
- A short exact sequence 0→M1→M2→M3→0 gives 0→I→M1⊗B→M2⊗B→M3⊗B→0 with I pseudo-null. Additivity of χ up to pseudo-null terms then gives φ(M2) = φ(M1) + φ(M3).
- The universal property (Prop. 11) gives a homomorphism θ: D(A) → D(B) with φ = θ∘χ_A.
- Checking on generators A/p: B_P/pB_P is zero unless P|p, and otherwise has length e(P/p) by definition of the ramification index. So θ = i.

(3) Rank formulas.
- (24), rank_B(M⊗B) = rank_A(M), is immediate by base change to L.
- The proof of (23), the formula for the content of a non-torsion module, begins: choose a free submodule H with torsion quotient Q, giving 0→I→H⊗B→M⊗B→Q⊗B→0 with I pseudo-null. The argument continues on the next typed sheet, which is not present here.

This typescript has no relation to the handwritten L-function computations on the adjacent pages.
errors: No mathematical errors. One implicit step is fine: every height-one P of B lies over a height-one p of A (true for integral extensions of Krull domains), which is what makes 'I_P = 0 for P|p' sufficient for pseudo-nullity.

ideas.what: Base change of an injection to the integral closure in a finite extension has pseudo-null kernel (flatness in codimension one).
ideas.modern_name: Flatness of the normalization in codimension one; Lemma 4 of Bourbaki AC VII §4

ideas.what: Compatibility of the content χ with extension of divisors: χ_B(M⊗B) = i(χ_A(M)), proved via ramification indices.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the characteristic ideal/divisor under integral extension (used e.g. in Iwasawa theory)

ideas.what: Rank invariance under base change to L.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused Bourbaki mimeographed draft (n° 392) of material published in Algèbre commutative Chap. VII. Its only historical interest is as evidence that Grothendieck wrote his L-function notes on the backs of Bourbaki drafts. That suggests the notes date from the early-to-mid 1960s, when such drafts circulated, which is consistent with the archive's '[à partir de 1962]'.
transcription_corrections: The page is typewritten (a Bourbaki duplicator draft), not a manuscript; the only handwriting is the archive foliation '53' in the lower left.
The kernel localization is written with underlined p (Fraktur/German p in typescript convention); 'I_P = (I_p)_P' is correct as transcribed.
In the sum, 'e_{P/p}.P' is typed as a subscript ramification index followed by a centered dot, i.e. Σ_{P|p} e_{P/p}·P.
